content:
sam: @channel seeing a sudden surge of 502/504s from hosted inference in eu-west since ~08:12 UTC. Multiple customer reports, some timeouts hitting 60s. Opening incident channel :rotating_light:

maria: grabbing traces and start grep across gateway logs now. any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: Canary deploy to eu-west-1 completed by ci-pipeline at 08:09:42 UTC (build: infra/2026-03-16-0810).

alex: seeing auth-proxy latency climbing before 5xxs. auth-proxy p95 went from ~120ms -> 3.2s starting 08:11. Could be upstreams or connpool exhaustion. :eyes:

jordan: kv-cache fill-rate spiked, TTL churn up ~08:11 as well — might be cache stampede on a hot prefix.

sam: ok, priority here: (1) collect a few failing request IDs, (2) roll traffic off eu-west if quick mitigation needed, (3) attempt auth-proxy restart if we suspect leaks.

lisa: posting a quick repro curl I got from customer A:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"test"}'

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"upstream read timeout","upstream":"inference-gateway-01"}
```

maria: gateway logs around 08:12 show repeated `upstream read timeout` and `connection reset by peer` to runtime pool nodes. snippet:

```
[2026-03-16T08:12:15Z] gateway eu-west request_id=xyz upstream=rt-12 timeout=60s error="upstream read timeout"
[2026-03-16T08:12:16Z] gateway eu-west request_id=abc upstream=rt-08 error="connection reset by peer"
```

sam: can we confirm evicted connections or OOMs on runtime side? alex/jordan can you check node metrics (conn count, fd usage, OOM killer)?

alex: runtime nodes show high socket backlog and many CLOSE_WAITs on rt-08/rt-12. memory stable, no OOM. fd usage ~78% on rt-12. connpool sizes bumped due to sudden concurrency.

jordan: kv-cache TTL churn caused hot partition; cache miss rate jumped 40% -> backend became overloaded with identical prefix requests (small prompts). We're seeing burst of identical prompts from a few customers.

lisa: customers affected: cust-A, cust-H, cust-K. cust-A sent logs showing repeated small prompts at very high QPS. Could be abusive client or bot.

sam: mitigation plan (short):
- rate-limit offending API keys (cust-A) temporarily :lock:
- scale up runtime pool in eu-west (add 4 nodes)
- clear hot kv-cache partitions and increase prefix cache size / TTL
- abort canary if suspected (deploy-bot)

maria: starting scale up now, requesting infra to spin 4x runtime eu-west, and increasing batcher worker count.

deploy-bot: Aborting canary deploy: infra/2026-03-16-0810 -> rollback initiated.

ops-bot: Rate limit applied to API key cust-A (soft limit 50r/s) by ops at 08:18 UTC.

alex: after rollback + rate-limit, 5xx rate dropped ~70% within 3m. auth-proxy latency back to baseline p95 ~150ms. still seeing occasional 502s from rt-12.

jordan: cleared hot prefixes and bumping kv-cache pool. miss rate down, backpressure reduced to runtime.

sam: good. keep monitoring for 30m. collect all request_ids for postmortem. also add temporary customer comms touchpoint to support.

lisa: I'll open a support thread with impacted customers summarizing mitigation and ETA for postmortem.

maria: immediate root-cause hypothesis: combination of a hot-client burst (identical prompts) + canary/rolling workload that reduced available capacity on the most-hit runtime nodes -> connpool pressure -> auth-proxy slowdowns -> gateway 502/504s.

alex: action items we should track:
- alex: add fd/socket and CLOSE_WAIT alerting for runtime nodes (P0)
- jordan: add prefix-level kv-cache metrics and hot-key detection (P1)
- maria: improve canary gating for traffic spikes during deploys; ensure canary doesn't land on high-traffic runtimes (P0)
- sam: create RB to auto-rate-limit keys that exceed token/QPS heuristics for short bursts (P2)
- lisa: customer outreach and postmortem draft (P1)

lisa: timeline and notes for postmortem:
- Incident start ~2026-03-16T08:12Z (first customer ping)
- Rollback initiated 08:17Z
- Rate-limits applied 08:18Z
- 5xxs dropped to baseline 08:21Z

sam: thanks everyone. tagging followups for tomorrow 10:00 UTC postmortem sync. please add any additional notes here. :thumbsup:

maria: adding logs + heap snapshots to the incident folder. will attach traces and request_id list in the postmortem doc.

jordan: planning small chaos test to simulate hot-key bursts against kv-cache next week.

alex: I'll open PR for close_wait alerting and quick dashboard for conn/FD usage.

lisa: postmortem assignees: alex (infra alerts), jordan (cache metrics), maria (canary gating & runtime tuning), sam (rate-limit automation), lisa (customer comms).

sam: last check: still some single-digit 502s but stable. closing incident channel here; keep thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
